title: slot-vigil-adaptive-surge-guard-and-sla-utilization-reporter
author: Olivia Park
release_notes: Introduces Slot Vigil surge guard with conservative default thresholds; new utilization reporting metrics (p99 headroom, slot-occupancy-histogram); opt-in rollout via feature flag; no API surface breaking changes.
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally see short, high-concurrency surges that exhaust per-tenant slot allocations and cause observation windows to underreport risk, resulting in SLA slippage. This PR implements 'Slot Vigil' — an adaptive surge guard that detects high-rate microbursts, soft-quarantines a small fraction of flexible slots, and surfaces a compact utilization synthesizer for closed-loop autoscalers. Design summary: 1) Surge detector that computes a short-window burst score using exponentially-weighted counts and inter-arrival variance; 2) Soft-quarantine mechanism that moves a small percentage of flexible slots into an emergency pool with a configurable release decay; 3) Elastic headroom predictor that reports p50/p95/p99 headroom per-tenant and per-pool, enabling autoscalers to factor in transient slack; 4) New telemetry: slot_vigil.burst_score, slot_vigil.quarantined_slots, telemetry.sla_headroom_p99, telemetry.slot_occupancy_histogram. Implementation notes: Most logic lives in serving/fleet/slot_vigil.go; quarantine bookkeeping persisted to etcd with TTLs; we added a lightweight local cache to avoid hot etcd hits during bursts. Config: feature flag enable_slot_vigil (default off), config knobs under fleet.autoscale.surge_guard.{sensitivity,quarantine_fraction,decay_seconds,min_release_batch}. Backwards compatibility: all behavior is opt-in behind the feature flag; default is no change to allocation. Tests and validation: unit tests for detector heuristics, integration test that replays synthetic microburst traces against a staging cluster (script in observability/test/replay_microbursts.sh), and end-to-end perf run showing 40-75% reduction in SLA violations during synthetic 10s microbursts at 3x baseline QPS. Rollout plan: 1) experimental rollout to Canary pool in us-west-2 (2 nodes) for 48h; 2) expand to 10% of dedicated capacity with monitoring dashboard; 3) full enablement after two successful 24h windows. Related work: ENG-2710 (autoscaler integration), ENG-2845 (tenant-level headroom metrics).

review_conversation: Ravi Nair (reviewer): The detector's sensitivity default seems aggressive; can we start with sensitivity=0.4? Also please add a rate-limiter around etcd writes to avoid hotloops.
Olivia Park (author): I lowered default sensitivity to 0.35 and added a 50ms jittered backoff on quarantine writes (serving/fleet/quarantine_store.go). Pushed fix in commit 9c6e1bf.
Marisol López (reviewer): Tests look good, but can we have a fail-open path if the quarantine store becomes unreachable? We should avoid hard failures in allocation path.
Olivia Park (author): Added fail-open: detector logs and skips quarantine when store errors exceed threshold; documented behavior in rfc and added unit test for degraded store path.
Eugene Kim (approver): Benchmarks are convincing for the synthetic storms. Please ensure console shows quarantine counts per-tenant before merging. Approved pending small docs tweak.
Olivia Park (author): Added dashboard widget and updated docs per feedback.
